data.name: rule.boot-degradation.evidence
data.value: Boot takes about {0}, the middle of the {1} most recent boots brisk could read from Windows' own timings. Windows blamed these for starting slower than it expected: {2} — that is how late each one was, not time it added to your boot. The bracketed figure is how many of those boots blamed it, so something that happens every start reads differently from a one-off, and a program blamed once may not start with Windows any more. Windows' own components often top the list and brisk will not switch those off; look for the rest under Startup programs on the Performance page.
